chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). A beggar came to him, so he gave him. Then another came, so he gave him. Then another came, so he gave him. Then another came, so he said: 'May Allah extend (wealth) upon you.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man had wealth amounting to thirty or forty thousand dirhams, and he desired that nothing of it should remain except that he place it in a rightful way, so he did it, and no wealth remained for himself, he would be among the three whose supplication is returned (unanswered).'

I said, 'Who are they?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One of them is a man who had wealth, so he spent it in other than its rightful way, then said, "O Lord, grant me sustenance." So He (Exalted is He) would say to him: "Did I not make for you a way to seek sustenance?"'

key_terms.غَيْرِ وَجْهِهِ: In other than its rightful way/improperly

ai.seo_question: Why is the supplication of some people returned unanswered despite their piety or requests?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the rejection of supplication stems not from poverty, but from the prior mismanagement of wealth, specifically spending it in 'non-rightful' ways (*ghayr wajhihi*). This highlights a key Shia ethical principle: the efficacy of *du'a* is contingent upon the moral integrity of one's economic conduct, as God’s response to the squanderer—'Did I not provide you with a means to seek sustenance?'—underscores personal responsibility in acquiring halal livelihood.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Al Waleed Bin sabeeh who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a beggar came over. So he<sup>asws</sup> gave him. Then another one came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> gave him. Then another one came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> gave him. Then another one came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Extend upon you’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a man, even if he had wealth reaching up to thirty or forty thousand Dirhams, then he so desires that there should not remain anything from it except that he should place it in a rightful way. So he does it, and there does not remain any wealth for himself, so he would happen to be from the three (kinds of people) whose supplications would be returned (unanswered)’.

I said, ‘Who are they?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One of them is a man who had wealth for him, so he spent it in other than its (rightful) way, then said, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace me’. So He<sup>azwj</sup> Would Say to him: “Did I not Make a way for you to seeking the livelihood?’
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when someone came asking for help. He gave him charity, then another one came, he gave him charity, yet another came for help, and he gave him charity. Then one more came for help and he said, ‘Allah will provide you.’

The Imam then said, ‘One may possess thirty or forty thousand dirham and then decide to spend it for a true cause until nothing is left with him. So he becomes one of the three kinds of people whose prayers are not heard.’

I then asked, ‘Who are such people?’ He replied, ‘One of them is a man who has a certain amount of wealth that he spends improperly and then prays to Allah for more wealth. He is then asked, “Have We not created ways and means to accumulate wealth?”’ (There is a mention of the other two kinds of people in al-Kafi, vol. 2, part 2, book of prayer Chapter 32 Hadith 1).
